I am 61 years old, went to primary school, and only started farming properly two years ago. Before that I worked outside, but now I am back on the land. My farm is 7.7 mu, not big, not small. I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same piece of land. My family has three people, but my son works in the city, so mostly it is me and my wife doing the work. I have a well, so when it gets dry I can pump water.

I do not know much book knowledge. What I know is from watching my neighbors and from doing it these two years. Last year my wheat got about 500 jin per mu, and my maize got about 550 jin per mu. That was okay, but I think I can do a little better if I manage it right. I do not want to lose yield. Fertilizer costs money, yes, but a bad harvest is much worse than wasting a bit of fertilizer.

**WHEAT:** I plant wheat in October. I will use an improved variety — I used Jimai 22 last year and it did fine, so I will stick with that. For the land, I will do rotary tillage before sowing, like everyone around here. I will put down basal fertilizer: I buy compound fertilizer from the dealer, about 100 jin per mu, the one with around 18-22-5 or similar. That gives me about 9 kg of nitrogen and 5 kg of phosphorus per mu in the basal. Then at green-up time in spring, I topdress with urea, about 50 jin per mu, which is another 11-12 kg of nitrogen. So in total my wheat gets about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus per mu, and maybe 3-4 kg potassium per mu from the compound. I will irrigate four times: winter irrigation after sowing if it is dry, then at green-up, then at jointing, and once more at flowering or grain-filling if the weather is hot and dry. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after sowing, then fungicide once in spring, and insecticide maybe once if I see bugs. That is three or four sprays total. I expect if the weather is normal, I can get around 550 kg per mu of wheat.

**MAIZE:** After I harvest wheat in early June, I sow maize right away without tillage — everyone here does no-tillage for summer maize, just sow straight into the wheat stubble. I will use Denghai 605, that hybrid seed. It costs more but the yield is good. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, about 80 jin per mu of the special compound, maybe 28-6-6 or 27-6-7. That gives me around 11 kg nitrogen, 2-3 kg phosphorus, and 2-3 kg potassium per mu. Some people add more urea at the big trumpet stage, but my neighbor Lao Wang says for his 7 mu he just uses the basal compound and gets good enough results, so I will do the same. If the leaves look yellow at trumpet stage, maybe I will add a little urea, but I am not sure yet, so I count it as just the basal for now. That is about 13 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potassium per mu total. I will irrigate twice: once at sowing if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet or flowering stage if there is no rain. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once, insecticide once or twice, and sometimes fungicide once. That is about three sprays. I expect around 600 kg per mu of maize if the weather cooperates.

I have to watch my money. Seed, fertilizer, water, chemicals — it all adds up. But I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing half my crop. Last year I spent too much on hired labor because my back was bad; this year I will try to do more myself to save money.
